Montréal Communiqué 


May 26th, 1971. 

The opportunities for Youth program has granted $9,000 for 
a project that will create 10-15 jobs and benefit some 1,000 black 
youngsters from the Cote des Neiges district. 

The urban camp undertaking, conceived jointly by a community 
group and the Montreal YMCA, also calls for each child to spend 
at least part of his vacation on a 750-acre farm made available by 
a private citizen. 

"Problems of the black community in Cote des Neiges 


' notes 


are similar to those of most immigrant minority groups,’ 
Leroy Butcher, the YMCA community worker in charge of the project. 

Butcher states that black peoples‘ efforts to adjust to 
society are made more complex by racism and its deep-rooted 
historical implications. 

"During the summer, we hope to lay the groundwork for a 
program that will involve the people in identifying their rights and 
responsibilities so they can help influence and create the 
institutions that affect them”, he says. 

The project will draw on the Y's experience in Mile End West, 


where thousands of immigrants--mainly from Greece-- have become 


involved in meeting both short-term and long-range concerns. 


MOTC.ces 


wilh 


The new summertime program in Cote des Neiges will be 
patterned after the Y's back alley work with children in Mile End 
West, where parents now help set policies and develop programs to 
meet the needs of their youngsters. 

Similar community involvement is planned for the Cote des 


Neiges project.
